Alright, let me switch gears a bit. As a stressed-out stay-at-home dad, I can definitely empathize with the challenges of caring for a newborn. Tantrums are a common part of their development, and it's important to remember that it's usually a sign of frustration rather than intentional misbehavior.

When my little one can't find their favorite toy, I try to redirect their attention by introducing a new toy or activity. If that doesn't work, I might try to comfort them by holding them, talking to them softly, or playing calming music. It's also essential to maintain a routine and provide plenty of sleep and nutrition to help reduce tantrums.

From a psychological perspective, understanding the developmental stages of infancy and toddlerhood can help parents respond appropriately to their child's behavior. It's important to remember that tantrums are a normal part of growing up, and with patience and consistency, they will pass.
